notes: dc CALL 2026-08-13: Q2 2026 call (Vélez, CFO Rob Livingston); AV EARNINGS_CALL_TRANSCRIPT hit the 25/day rate limit on the single probe; transcript read via Motley Fool page as a summary (search_excerpt), not verbatim.

dc FORM Nu is a 20-F/6-K filer; the Q2 release (6-K) is the managerial view, the IFRS financial statements (6-K) are the audited-basis view. Managerial net income equals IFRS net income (1,061.1m) but revenue (5,875.7 vs 5,513.2m), funding cost, cost of credit (1,690.8 vs 1,482.2m) and taxes (revenue-based taxes 240.9m moved above gross profit; income taxes 569.2 managerial vs 175.2 IFRS) are reclassified: use one basis per ratio. Growth rates in the release are FX neutral; IFRS USD growth differs (revenue +50% y/y IFRS USD).

dc FACT IFRS Q2 2026 (USD m): total revenue 5,513.2 (Q2 25: 3,668.5); interest income and gains 4,760.6; fee and commission income 752.6; ECL 1,482.2 (1,012.2); gross profit 2,346.5 (1,548.0); G&A 599.8; income before tax 1,236.3; income taxes 175.2 (effective rate 14.2%; Q2 25: 27.6%); net income 1,061.1 (637.0); diluted EPS 0.2162 (0.1300); diluted weighted shares 4,904.8m.

dc FACT IFRS balance sheet 2026-06-30 (USD m): total assets 82,753; 'loans to customers' statement line 11,317 (excludes credit card receivables shown elsewhere; the 39.4bn managerial portfolio is the headline); deposits 45,328 (Dec 25: 41,925); borrowings and financing 4,682 (4,398); repurchase agreements 1,058; payables to network 15,542; cash and cash equivalents 13,552 (includes funds that back deposits: not spendable corporate liquidity); securities 3,777; compulsory deposits at central banks 9,149; total equity 13,252 (Dec 25: 11,322); total liabilities 69,502; lease liabilities 66.

dc FACT Six months to 2026-06-30: net income 1,932.5m (1,194.2m); ECL 3,200.2m (1,985.7m); interest received 5,976m; income tax paid 1,789m. Q1 2026 derived as six months minus Q2: revenue 4,968.0m, gross profit 1,864.9m, net income 871.4m.

dc FACT Geography: Brazil 91.1% of Q2 26 IFRS revenue interest-and-fee basis (3,990.3 of 4,380.9m), Mexico 7.2% (314.6m, +79% y/y), other 1.7%. No customer is 10% or more of revenue (note 34 segment information; one reportable segment, CODM is the CEO).

dc FACT Mexico bank: CNBV operations authorization notified 2026-07-09 (license obtained 2025-04-24); began operating as a multiple bank 2026-08-06. 15.8m customers in Q2, 16m in July. Mexico deposits 5.7bn, loan-to-deposit 35%, deposits declining modestly by design (deposit optimization).

dc FACT Brazil banking license: 2026-07-20 share purchase agreement to acquire 100% of Banco Porto Real de Investimentos S.A. to add a banking license (Joint Resolution No. 17 brand-name rule); subject to Central Bank of Brazil approval; price not disclosed in the notes; no additional capital or liquidity requirement claimed. Colombia: Nu Colombia Compania de Financiamiento (financing company, not a bank): 5m+ customers, deposits 3.3bn.

dc FACT Capital return: Board approved on 2026-06-03 a US$1.0bn buyback for 12 months from 2026-06-04; 40.66m Class A shares bought for US$500.4m in Q2 (avg about US$12.31), held in treasury, 499.6m remaining; no dividend.
dc FACT Subsequent: 2026-10-23 6-K: CTO Eric Young resigns (stays to 2026-11-12); CEO Vélez and CISO John Walton interim; search under way. Not a number; a management-depth item.

dc MGMT Release (2026-08-13): net income above US$1bn for the first time, ROE 33%, 'more than a billion dollars in quarterly net income'; Mexico bank launched, 'largest digital bank in the country with 16 million customers'; NuFormer foundation model in production on three portfolios (cards Brazil and Mexico, unsecured Brazil), SME and Colombia cards in test; AI agents handle over 60% of Brazil support conversations; Croma tier for Super Core launched July.

dc MGMT Release: efficiency ratio rose to 19.5% from 17.6% because real estate and marketing costs shifted from Q1 into Q2 plus international expansion; 15-90 NPL improved 16 bps to 4.8% mostly seasonality, 'partially offset by intentional expansions into higher-risk, higher-return segments'; 90+ NPL +35 bps to 6.9% on seasonal migration of Q1 early delinquencies; NIM +180 bps to 22.9% on portfolio growth, mix toward unsecured and the risk expansions announced last quarter; cost of credit -9% q/q.

dc MGMT Call (summary, secondary): efficiency ratio to average about 20% for 2026 and Q1's 17.6% not a run rate; risk-adjusted NIM expected 'in the same region' (CFO did not call 12% a floor); allowance 6.6bn, 90+ coverage 244%; Desenrola renegotiation program touched cost of credit by about 5% (1.8m customers); US entry spend capped at about 100 bps of efficiency ratio, US credit models 12 to 30 months; headcount about 10,400, US hiring from about 1% to 2%; underwriting assumes conditions worse than history; private payroll lending described as an asymmetric bet, scaled slowly. Not issuer numeric guidance: no revenue or earnings guidance is issued.

dc GUIDANCE Nu issues no numeric revenue, NIM, cost-of-risk or earnings guidance in the release; only the call statements above (efficiency ratio about 20% FY2026, risk-adjusted NIM same region). Track record from guidance therefore unavailable (gap).
dc RISK Credit risk management failure (20-F Item 3.D summary): unsecured and card lending in high-rate Brazil; 90+ NPL 6.9% and intentional expansion into higher-risk segments (release).
dc RISK International expansion (Mexico, Colombia, US plans) may not succeed or may carry added risk (20-F 3.D summary; release: efficiency ratio pressure from expansion).

dc RISK Regulation: extensive oversight as payment institution; pending Brazilian Congress, BCB and Ministry of Finance initiatives on payments and finance; tax law changes (20-F 3.D summary). Brazil banking license is being added via Banco Porto Real, pending BCB approval.

dc RISK Macro and rates: FX and interest-rate instability, Brazil government influence; Brazilian presidential elections October 2026 flagged in the 20-F as a volatility source (20-F 3.D summary). Q3 results (mid-November, not yet out at as_of) will show the election-period read.
dc RISK Technology: dependence on IT systems and third-party data centers and clouds; AI-use legal, reputational and cost risks (20-F 3.D summary); CTO resignation 2026-10-23.
dc RISK Brand and concentration of control: brand reliance; founder David Vélez holds 88.3% of Class B shares and about 74.4% of voting power (20-F 3.D summary, 2025 report).

dc RISK Income tax rate: IFRS effective rate 14.2% in Q2 26 vs 27.6% in Q2 25; part of the y/y net income growth (+67% IFRS) comes from the lower rate; managerial view puts income taxes at 569.2m (35%): check which the net income rests on.

dc GAP Q3 2026 results are not out at as_of 2026-11-01 (Nu reports mid-November); no 10-Q equivalent exists for a 20-F filer, so no quarterly 10-Q reading file; the 6-K IFRS statements serve instead. Cost-of-risk as a percentage and 90+ NPL by cohort, CET1/capital ratios and Brazil Selic exposure were not extracted.
